primary_diagnosis: Secondary hypertension (primary aldosteronism, renal-artery stenosis, obstructive sleep apnea)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with resistant stage 2 hypertension, early CKD, anemia, COPD, and dyslipidemia. Red‑flag features and the absence of targeted secondary work‑up make secondary hypertension the most likely primary diagnosis. Hypertensive nephrosclerosis and heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia are also strongly supported by the chronic hypertension and lipid profile. Diabetes‑related kidney disease is possible but undermined by an implausibly low HbA1c. Additional findings such as urine bilirubin, opioid use without indication, and modest proteinuria broaden the differential but carry lower probabilities.
unresolved_findings: Urine bilirubin 1.4 mg/dL (no liver function tests or hemolysis work‑up)
Opioid prescription without documented pain diagnosis
recommended_workup: Plasma aldosterone concentration and plasma renin activity (screen for primary aldosteronism)
Renal artery duplex ultrasound or CT/MRA to evaluate for renal‑artery stenosis
Overnight polysomnography to assess for obstructive sleep apnea
Comprehensive lipid panel and initiation of statin therapy if LDL remains elevated
Repeat HbA1c and fasting glucose or oral glucose tolerance test to verify diabetic status
Serum creatinine, eGFR calculation, and urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio for CKD staging
Liver function tests (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT, total bilirubin) and hemolysis panel (LDH, haptoglobin, peripheral smear) to clarify urine bilirubin
Pulmonary function tests (spirometry) to grade COPD severity
Review opioid prescription, assess pain documentation, and consider urine drug screen
Renal biopsy if proteinuria persists and etiology remains unclear
